$comment: New Zealand, Treaty of Waitangi jurisprudence - the constitutional status of a 'principles of the Treaty of Waitangi' clause, and the Supreme Court's confirmation that the Court of Appeal's 1987 paramount-provision reading applies to all subsequent equivalent clauses. The originating 1987 case (the 'Lands case') is not itself independently fetched - the researching agent used the citing-judgment method via the 2013 Supreme Court sequel, which quotes and applies it directly with pinpoint paragraph references, consistent with the approach used elsewhere in this repository for older cases.
verification_method: State-Owned Enterprises Act 1986 s.9 - legislation.govt.nz presented a 'Human Verification' bot-check gate, and NZLII's mirror of the Act is only available as an unrenderable scanned PDF; the exact text was corroborated via the Supreme Court's own verbatim quotation of it in New Zealand Maori Council v Attorney-General [2013] NZSC 6 at para 34, and independently confirmed via WebSearch against a genuine secondary source. New Zealand Maori Council v Attorney-General [2013] NZSC 6 - the researching agent fetched the full judgment directly from NZLII; this session's own independent re-fetch of the same NZLII URL returned HTTP 403.

authorities.name: State-Owned Enterprises Act 1986, s.9
authorities.date_note: Enactment year - the first of what became a recurring statutory clause pattern in later New Zealand legislation requiring Crown consistency with Treaty principles. Not independently re-fetched at the raw legislation.govt.nz page level this session - see verification_note.
authorities.proposition: Nothing in the Act shall permit the Crown to act in a manner that is inconsistent with the principles of the Treaty of Waitangi. A short, unqualified clause that New Zealand courts have construed as a paramount constitutional constraint on the Crown's exercise of its statutory powers, not merely aspirational language subordinate to the Act's other machinery provisions.
authorities.verification_note: legislation.govt.nz presented an active bot-check gate to the researching agent's attempts, and NZLII's mirror of this historical Act is only available as a scanned, unrenderable PDF. The exact text was instead confirmed via the citing-judgment method: the Supreme Court's own verbatim quotation of s.9 at paragraph 34 of New Zealand Maori Council v Attorney-General [2013] NZSC 6, corroborated by an independent Wikipedia article quoting identical wording. This session's own independent WebSearch further confirmed the identical text via a genuine secondary source (legislation.govt.nz's own indexed page title, and the Te Ara Encyclopedia of New Zealand).

authorities.name: New Zealand Maori Council v Attorney-General
authorities.judge_or_panel: Elias CJ, McGrath J, William Young J, Chambers J, Glazebrook J (unanimous, single opinion)
authorities.proposition: Adopts and generalises the Court of Appeal's 1987 construction of s.9 (New Zealand Maori Council v Attorney-General [1987] 1 NZLR 641, the 'Lands case', quoted directly at paras 55-59) as a paramount provision with 'strong and unambiguous language' having an overriding effect on the rest of the Act - and holds that this reading 'must accordingly form the basis of the approach of New Zealand courts to any subsequent legislation requiring that the Crown act consistently with Treaty principles,' giving 'no support to narrow approaches to the meaning of such clauses.' Applying this to a proposed partial privatisation of a state-owned power company, the Court held Crown action under such a clause is reviewable for Treaty consistency, but the practical touchstone is whether the action would materially impair the Crown's ability to remedy any Treaty breach - on the facts, the proposed share sale would not, so the appeal was dismissed.
authorities.verification_note: The researching agent fetched the full judgment directly from NZLII, confirmed by page title matching the citation and cross-checked against courtsofnz.govt.nz's own case listing, quoting paragraphs 34-35, 55-59, and 7-9 verbatim. This session's own independent re-fetch of the same NZLII URL returned HTTP 403, so the pinpoint quotes were not independently re-confirmed a second time by this session, though the researching agent's own fetch was a genuine primary-source read, not a proxy.

edges.verified_via: New Zealand Maori Council v Attorney-General [2013] NZSC 6, paras 34-35, 55-59, per the researching agent's direct NZLII fetch: adopts the 1987 Court of Appeal's paramount-provision construction of s.9 as the governing template for all equivalent Treaty-principles clauses in subsequent legislation, and applies a material-impairment-of-remedy test to the facts.

what_this_is_not: Two nodes covering the constitutional status of a Treaty-principles clause and its general application - New Zealand's fourth populated Authority Graph entry in this repository. Does not independently verify the 1987 Lands case's own primary text (accessed only via citation inside the 2013 sequel), the substantive content of 'the principles of the Treaty' themselves (partnership, active protection, etc.) in detail, or any other Treaty of Waitangi jurisprudence subject - all remain unbuilt.
